## Natural history notes

A small seedworm moth characterized by narrow grayish-brown to reddish-brown forewings with subtle pale bands and mottled markings typical of many tortricid moths. In Florida, it is associated with longleaf pine habitats such as pine flatwoods, sandhills, open pine woodlands, and managed pine stands where longleaf pine cones are present. The caterpillars develop inside pine cones and feed on seeds or cone tissue, while adults are small, mostly nocturnal moths that may be overlooked unless reared from cones or attracted to lights.
